metadatos-pdf.title: PDF Metadata Editor
metadatos-pdf.description: Edit the hidden title, author, subject, and keywords in your PDF. Free, no account, and the file never leaves your device.
metadatos-pdf.cta: Need to clean up metadata across hundreds of documents for your business? We can build that automation for you.
metadatos-pdf.seoTitle: Free Online PDF Metadata Editor Tool | SonhoLab
metadatos-pdf.seoDescription: Edit a PDF's title, author, and keywords for free in seconds. Everything runs in your browser, so the file never uploads to any server. No signup.
metadatos-pdf.intro: Every PDF carries hidden data beyond what shows up on the page: who created it, when, and under what title. Those fields — title, author, subject, and keywords — often end up with generic names like Document1 or the Windows username of whoever generated the file, and they show up as-is whenever someone opens the file or saves it to their computer. Here you upload the PDF, see those four fields already filled in with whatever the file currently has, edit them as needed, and download a copy with the updated metadata. Everything happens right in your browser: the PDF never leaves your device.
metadatos-pdf.stepsHeading: How to edit a PDF's metadata in 3 steps
metadatos-pdf.step1Text: Drag the file into the upload area or select it from your device. The tool automatically reads the title, author, subject, and keywords already saved in the file and displays them in an editable form.
metadatos-pdf.step2Text: Replace the title with one that actually describes the document, fix the author field if it still shows a former employee's name or your computer's username, and add keywords to make the file easier to find later.
metadatos-pdf.step3Text: Click download and a copy of the PDF is generated with the new metadata, ready to send. The content on the pages stays exactly the same — only the file's hidden information changes.
metadatos-pdf.useCase1: A freelancer double-checks a proposal before sending it to a client and finds the author field still says Untitled-Final-v3-COPY instead of their name or studio.
metadatos-pdf.useCase2: Someone organizing a company's PDF library gives every file a consistent, descriptive title and keywords so they're easy to search later.
metadatos-pdf.useCase3: A student submitting an assignment wants the PDF's author to show their own name instead of the shared computer at the library where they wrote it.
metadatos-pdf.faq1q: Which PDF metadata fields can I edit with this tool?
metadatos-pdf.faq1a: You can edit four standard fields: title, author, subject, and keywords. These are the values many programs show as the browser tab name or in a file preview, and they can quietly reveal who created the document or what software was used.
metadatos-pdf.faq2q: Does this change the visible text or content on the pages?
metadatos-pdf.faq2a: No. It only changes the file's invisible metadata, not what's printed on the pages themselves. If you need to fix something inside the actual document text, you'll need another tool for that before adjusting the metadata here.
metadatos-pdf.faq3q: Does it also remove GPS location or edit history from the PDF?
metadatos-pdf.faq3a: It doesn't, and usually there's nothing to remove: unlike a photo, a PDF typically doesn't carry GPS coordinates. Some editors do embed an internal revision history, but this tool is scoped specifically to the four standard metadata fields, not that kind of extra data.
metadatos-pdf.faq4q: Does my PDF get uploaded to a server to edit its metadata?
metadatos-pdf.faq4a: No. The file is processed entirely inside your browser, using the pdf-lib library running on your own device. It never travels to our servers or anyone else's, so you can use it on sensitive documents without worrying about that.
metadatos-pdf.faq5q: Is it free, and do I need to create an account?
metadatos-pdf.faq5a: It's free and doesn't ask for an account or an email address. You can edit the metadata of one PDF or twenty in the same day, with no limits and no watermark, because there's no server cost to pass on to you.
